    return True

def find_header_col(ws, header_names):
    header_names_lower = {h.lower() for h in header_names}

                return cell.row, cell.column

    """
    If workbook already contains an obvious green/red fill, reuse it;
    otherwise use standard Excel conditional-formatting colors.
    """
    candidates = []
    for ws in wb.worksheets:
        for row in ws.iter_rows():
            for cell in row:
                fill = cell.fill
                if fill and fill.fill_type and fill.fgColor and fill.fgColor.type == "rgb" and fill.fgColor.rgb:
                    rgb = fill.fgColor.rgb[-6:].upper()
                    try:
                        r, g, b = int(rgb[0:2], 16), int(rgb[2:4], 16), int(rgb[4:6], 16)
                    except Exception:
                        continue
                    if target == "green" and g > r and g > b:
                        candidates.append(fill)
                    elif target == "red" and r > g and r > b:
                        candidates.append(fill)
    if candidates:
